findings.finding: The `PLUGIN_ROOT` discriminator is not a reliable Claude/Codex boundary. It's an ordinary inherited environment variable: if a user's shell (or a wrapper script) happens to export `PLUGIN_ROOT`, all three new hooks become live in Claude sessions too — precisely the regression AC0 exists to prevent. Conversely, there's no check that the value of `PLUGIN_ROOT` points at this bundle, so any other plugin's Codex run (or a stray value) arms the mint/gate path for a session that may not be an iterate launch.
findings.suggestion: Cheap hardening: in `is_codex_runtime()`, verify `PLUGIN_ROOT` resolves to (or contains) the expected bundle root — one extra comparison. Also have the AC0 fixture test the "wrong `PLUGIN_ROOT` value" case, not just absence. This doesn't change the fail-open contract; it tightens the deny path's precondition.

findings.finding: The armed-Stop-loop trap: an armed session that never runs `setup_iterate_worktree.py` (user aborts the iterate, or Codex goes off-script) will hit the Stop gate on every turn-end with no worktree pointer → repair always fails → block, every turn, until the consecutive-block cap trips. The cap is the only escape, and the plan doesn't say whether the counter resets after a successful (allowed) Stop — if it does, the session can oscillate block/allow/block indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Make the block-counter session-scoped and monotonic (never reset by an allowed Stop), and make the failure reason text explicitly instruct the model to either run setup or have the operator disarm — a self-describing exit, not just a cap.

findings.finding: The `PreToolUse` first-call gate denies any non-setup tool call, including harmless ones Codex may legitimately want first (`ls`, reading a file to orient). Every such denial is recoverable (deny + reason → Codex retries after setup), but the gate denies repeatedly until the setup call appears, and there's no stated deny-budget. A confused model could burn many turns retrying the same disallowed first call.
findings.suggestion: Either include the setup invocation verbatim in the deny reason (likely intended — make it an explicit AC detail so the fixture asserts the reason contains the exact runnable command), and/or document expected behavior after N denials. No new mechanism needed; just pin the reason-string contract in the fixture.

findings.finding: The `.consumed` exclusive-create and the "first-call-settled" flag are described as separate primitives but their interaction isn't specified: does settling the first-call flag consume the activation record, or only the setup-match? If the record's expiry elapses mid-session (plan says expired → fail-open), then a later Stop gate sees no armed record — good — but the Stop gate reads what, exactly, when the record was consumed by the PreToolUse hook? The boundary table says the gate reads the completion event, but the loop-breaker counter is "stored beside the activation record" — if the record is consumed/deleted, where does the counter live?
findings.suggestion: Specify the record's lifecycle explicitly: consume should mark, not delete, and the counter should live in a session-scoped path independent of the armed record's lifetime.

findings.finding: iterate_stop_finalize.py` remains in the Codex Stop chain (shared `hooks.json`, no `PLUGIN_ROOT` guard on it). The plan asserts its freshness gate makes it idempotent against the new gate's repair, but the stop-gate fixtures only test the pair in one ordering. If Codex's Stop payload differs in a way the existing hook doesn't expect (e.g., missing a field it gates on), its behavior under Codex is untested by AC0.
findings.suggestion: Add the payload-capture probe output for a Stop event to the evidence, and add one fixture (or live-probe assertion) that `iterate_stop_finalize.py` under a Codex-shaped Stop payload either no-ops or fails safely.

findings.finding: Step 11's "if (c) or (d) fails, the Stop gate must not ship armed" is a real stop condition, but the plan doesn't define the fallback artifact: if Codex ignores `decision: block` on Stop, does the hook ship in `hooks.json` unarmed (guard flag?), or is it excluded from the bundle? An undefined fallback invites a half-wired hook.
findings.suggestion: Pre-commit to the fallback: hook shipped but short-circuited by a build/config flag (e.g., an `enabled` key checked at hook start), with the probe outcome recorded in the docs delta either way.

findings.finding: The mint hook is described as writing an armed/unarmed marker on every `UserPromptSubmit`, but the gate is intended to be determined by the first prompt only. A later ordinary prompt could overwrite an armed record with `armed: false`, or introduce an envelope after the session has already begun.
findings.suggestion: Make initial activation immutable per session/generation: exclusively create it on the first submission, never overwrite it, and explicitly reject or ignore envelopes on later submissions. Define how “first prompt” is determined if the live payload has no prompt ordinal.

findings.finding: The Stop-gate design does not say it consumes and validates the activation record before repairing/blocking. As written, every Codex-runtime Stop event using this iterate hook registration could attempt finalization and potentially block—even unarmed sessions, unrelated turns, or sessions without a valid run identity. This conflicts with the stated fail-open scope.
findings.suggestion: Require a valid, unexpired `armed: true` record matching the current session, turn, normalized worktree, and generation before any Stop enforcement. Treat absent, unarmed, expired, or mismatched records as a visible fail-open path.

findings.finding: The record schema lists session/turn/cwd/generation/expiry, while the Stop completion predicate requires `adr_id=run_id`. The plan never defines where `run_id` is persisted, how it is bound to the activation record, or how the Stop payload resolves it.
findings.suggestion: Add `run_id` (and preferably activation/start timestamp or generation) to the record’s validated schema, sourced from the parsed envelope. Match completion events using the existing oracle’s complete freshness/worktree rules, not only the three event fields, so an older event for a reused run ID cannot satisfy the gate.

findings.finding: The tool policy is precise only for shell-command matching. It references `spawn_agent`/`Agent` classes in the inventory but does not define which local function tools are eligible, how their payloads are parsed, or whether they are denied before setup. That leaves a practical bypass if a non-shell local tool can proceed before the required worktree command.
findings.suggestion: After the live capture, codify a complete allow/deny matrix for every locally hook-visible tool name and input shape. Default unknown local function-tool classes to deny while armed and unsettled; only the specifically parsed setup command should settle the gate.

findings.finding: The required live checks are procedural only. The implementation remains automatically armed after bundle installation, so a failed or skipped Stop-block/order probe could still be distributed despite the stated “must not ship armed” condition. The probe is also version-specific to Codex CLI 0.155.0.
findings.suggestion: Introduce an explicit Stop-enforcement capability flag that defaults off in distributable configuration and is enabled only with recorded successful evidence for the supported CLI version range. Add an upgrade/revalidation requirement when the supported Codex hook runtime changes.

findings.finding: The persisted loop-breaker counter lacks defined identity, atomic update behavior, reset rules, and cleanup. Concurrent Stop deliveries or a stale counter could either block repeatedly or fail open for a later legitimate turn.
findings.suggestion: Scope the counter to the validated activation generation and turn, update it atomically, set a bounded expiry, and test concurrent Stop invocations plus a new turn reusing the same session/worktree.

findings.finding: The activation files and consumed markers are enforcement inputs in a predictable workspace path. Any process able to modify that workspace can write `armed: false`, a consumed marker, or a completion event. The spec accepts no nonce, but the helper’s Windows quoting approach also remains unspecified and could introduce command injection if it invokes a shell.
findings.suggestion: Document this explicitly as cooperative local-process enforcement, validate/sanitize all payload-derived path components, keep records free of full prompt content, and implement the helper using an argument-vector process launch rather than shell-built command text.  The core mechanism is sound and the plan has already addressed several important hook-runtime risks. It should be revised to make first-prompt activation immutable and to bind Stop enforcement, event freshness, and loop-breaking to a concrete armed run identity.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

Addressed as an accepted residual risk of the same cooperative-enforcement threat model already accepted for the matcher's basename-only bypass, extended to a dispatch-concurrency assumption. Codex's actual PreToolUse dispatch concurrency (batched/parallel calls, retries) is unconfirmed; documented in hook-inventory.md as a second required question for R2b's deferred live probe rather than guessed at now.

Claim under doubt: the hooks-codex/hooks.json split makes the two Tier-3 hooks cost zero process-spawns under Claude Code — This was asserted, not verified, in the diff -- no probe confirmed Claude Code's real loader ignores hooks-codex/hooks.json, and the repo has been burned before by wrong assumptions in this exact area.

Claim under doubt: the activation-record mechanism is a self-contained, low-footprint addition with no ongoing cost beyond the session it protects — codex_activation_record.py had no purge/GC path at all -- every session's record + .consumed sidecar persisted forever, invisible to the bloat gate since it's gitignored, unlike the sibling event_once.py primitive which already has _purge_expired_claims.

Claim under doubt: moving the two Tier-3 hooks Codex-only keeps their per-invocation cost minimal on the runtime that actually needs them — Both mint() and consume() unconditionally re-normalized cwd (a git subprocess) and rebuilt/re-derived state on every single call for the whole session, even long after settlement -- the mechanism zeroed cost under Claude but did not minimize it under Codex.

This is exactly the "false-deny on legitimate variants" class the internal plan review's finding 11 required the matcher to avoid; the shipped hint happens to place flags after the script, but `uv run --project <path> <script>` is common real usage.

Every `PreToolUse` call in an armed Codex session still spawns a git process for the whole session, which is precisely the cost the doubt review flagged.
findings.suggestion: Move the exists()-style short-circuit above the normalize (e.g., cache per-session project_root keyed on raw cwd, or make the `.consumed` existence check reachable before normalization), or correct the inventory's "FIXED" claim to state the residual per-call git cost honestly.

findings.finding: The `mkdir` call is outside the OSError guard, so an unwritable/read-only project root makes `mint()`/`consume()` raise, violating the module docstring's hard contract ("fail-open… never an exception"). findings.suggestion: Wrap the `mkdir` in the same `try: … except OSError: return None` as the `os.open`, or use `_exists_fail_open`-style suppression.

AC0's text also still says "any of the three new hooks" although the Stop-gate cut leaves two.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line correction to mini-plan §1/step 8 pointing at the `hooks-codex` registration (the run's own convention for post-hoc plan corrections), and fix the "three" count in AC0.

findings.finding: The spec's verification commands cover only two test roots (`shared/tests` and `plugins/shipwright-iterate/tests`), but this run added tests in a third root: `test_codex_activation_helper.py`, `test_codex_activation_helper_guards.py`, `test_codex_hook_inventory_runtime_scope.py`, plus launcher/fixture changes in `shared/scripts/tools/tests/`. (The round-2 spec-review already noted the missing matcher file; this is the same gap one size larger.)
findings.suggestion: Add the `shared/scripts/tools/tests` invocation (or a `-k` selector for the new files) to the Verification section's runner commands.

findings.finding: If the mint hook fails (any exception → silent exit 0), the gate sees an absent record and silently allows with no visibility — the unarmed-warning path only covers the minted `armed: false` record, not "mint never happened".
